subject: Kyoto-mini (2B) onboarding: telemetry hooks and temporary pin request
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.example>
To: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.example>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.example>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.example>, onboarding@kyoto.ai
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Kyoto-mini (2B) onboarding: telemetry hooks and temporary pin request

Team / Kyoto onboarding,

Quick summary: Kyoto has delivered kyoto-mini v1.2 (2B) which looks promising for low-cost hosted routes. Early staging runs show tokenization edge-cases and a 2x P95 latency bump under continuous-batch warmup. Before we expose this to any customers we need:

- A short compatibility checklist (tokenizer/KV cache/quantization) completed by infra.
- A short telemetry schema from Kyoto so we can validate model-side logs.
- A temporary version pin (kyoto-mini@v1.2) for 72 hours in staging+canary while we validate metrics and run fallback trials.

Why the pin: without a pin, our routing may flip between kyoto-mini v1.1 (their internal default) and v1.2 during parallel rollouts. We need a stable variant to run deterministic checks (safety evals, replay tests, and prefix-cache behavior).

What I need from each of you:
- Dev (dev): can you list the failing compatibility checks you saw and whether they are quick fixes or require infra changes?
- Laura (product): do we approve a 72-hour temporary pin for canary routes? If yes, what SLA exceptions/notifications do you want?
- Hannah (security/compliance): confirm if the telemetry payload Kyoto proposes is acceptable from a PII/PHI perspective; we should avoid sampling raw prompts.

Attaching: kyoto-mini-v1.2-metadata.json and Kyoto's sample telemetry (they dropped a CSV).

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.example

Attachments: kyoto-mini-v1.2-metadata.json (json), kyoto-telemetry-sample.csv (csv)

From: Dev Patel <dev@redwood.example>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.example>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.example>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.example>, onboarding@kyoto.ai
Date: Sun, 20 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kyoto-mini (2B) onboarding: telemetry hooks and temporary pin request

On Sun, Sep 20, 2026 at 09:12 AM Ben Carter <ben@redwood.example> wrote:
> Team / Kyoto onboarding,
> 
> Quick summary: Kyoto has delivered kyoto-mini v1.2 (2B) which looks promising for low-cost hosted routes. Early staging runs show tokenization edge-cases and a 2x P95 latency bump under continuous-batch warmup. Before we expose this to any customers we need:
> ...

Thanks Ben — digging in. Short technical notes from the staging run (staging cluster: s-us-east-3):

1) Tokenization mismatch: kyoto-mini uses a slightly different BOS/EOS encoding and their subword split differs on common tokens (we see ~0.6% tokenization mismatch on our internal eval set). This causes length and score diffs for replay tests.

2) KV cache alignment: their implementation pads differently which means our continuous-batch merging heuristic miscomputes effective cache size in the early steps and triggers a fallback that increases latency.

3) Quantization profile: they included int8 weights, but our kernels need a small shim to support their quant-format (per-channel scales). I can prototype the shim in ~1.5d, but we'd prefer Kyoto provide a tokenizer.json and a small mapping file so we don't patch the runtime long-term.

Proposed acceptance criteria for canary before unpinning:
- P95 latency on 4k seq synthetic < 180ms for single-token completion in canary (baseline is 120ms).
- Peak GPU memory < 22GB for continuous-batch at target concurrency.
- Tokenization mismatch rate < 0.3% across our core eval prompts after applying tokenizer mapping.
- No safety regression on our 1k prompt eval (false positive/negative delta < 0.5%).

Operational ask: I support a 72-hour temporary pin on the canary path if Kyoto provides tokenizer.json and the telemetry sample contains per-request latency and quantization metadata (scale/zero_point per-layer). Also need a short rollback runbook (I can produce).

Dev
Dev Patel
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev@redwood.example

From: Izumi Tanaka <izumi@kyoto.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.example>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.example>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.example>
Cc: onboarding@kyoto.ai
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 08:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kyoto-mini (2B) onboarding: telemetry hooks and temporary pin request

Hi Ben / Dev / team,

Thanks for the detailed notes and for trying v1.2. A few items from our side: we can produce an export of tokenizer.json and a token-mapping patch (attached as tokenizer-mapping.patch). The telemetry_sample.csv we shared includes per-request: request_id, model_version, latency_ms, gpu_mem_mb, quant_format, per_layer_scale_count. Link: https://s3.amazonaws.com/kyoto-artifacts/kyoto-mini/v1.2/telemetry_sample.csv

Notes:
- v1.2 uses a compact BPE variant; tokenizer.json will align exactly to how we canonicalize BOS/EOS. The mapping patch will convert edge-case tokens that differ from the Redwood tokenization.
- For quantization we are supplying an int8 per-channel file; we've verified functional parity on our internal evals.
- We are OK with the temporary 72-hour pin for canary, and will provide a signed manifest listing exact artifact hashes for v1.2 (so you can detect any accidental swap).

Attachments: tokenizer-mapping.patch (diff), kyoto-telemetry-sample.csv (csv)

Izumi Tanaka
Head of Model Ops, Kyoto AI
izumi@kyoto.ai

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.example>
To: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.example>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.example>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.example>
Cc: Izumi Tanaka <izumi@kyoto.ai>
Date: Mon, 21 Sep 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Kyoto-mini (2B) onboarding: telemetry hooks and temporary pin request

Laura / Hannah — tagging you for formal approvals:

Summary of current state:
- Kyoto provided tokenizer mapping and telemetry sample (attached), and agreed to manifest + artifact hashes.
- Dev estimates ~1.5d to prototype a small shim; but if we accept Kyoto's tokenizer.json we can avoid a runtime patch.

Request: I propose we do a controlled temporary pin of kyoto-mini@v1.2 on the following scope:
- Duration: 72 hours (start window: 2026-09-22 02:00 UTC).
- Scope: staging -> 5% canary traffic in us-west and us-east routing pools.
- Acceptance: Dev's criteria (P95 < 180ms, mem < 22GB, token mismatch < 0.3%, safety delta < 0.5%).
- Rollback: automatic on metric breach (alert -> immediate rollback to kyoto-mini@v1.1 + oncall page).

Hannah: confirm telemetry schema is acceptable (we must strip raw prompt text; request-level hashes ok). If you'd rather we collect aggregated stats only, say so and we will restrict.

Laura: please confirm product ok to grant the temporary pin and the canary scope. If approved I will file the pin request and schedule the rollout with infra.

Ben
Ben Carter
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.example
